textBlocks.content:
March 12, 1981

Today's wind came down from the North Mountain Pass, carrying the smell of mine dust.

I turned through the duty logbook again. Some of the words on the page about the northern mountain road had been blurred by the rain.

March 18, 1981

The light on the mountaintop turned on once during the night.

It was not an inspection light, and it did not look like a truck light either. It stayed on the ridge, as if waiting for someone to look back.

stickyNoteSlots.noteContent: The north mountain road was not just a shortcut. Someone once ran toward the mountain from here, and Grandpa kept writing about that same ridge years later.

textBlocks.content:
April 2, 1981

The office window was cracked, and an old employee badge was still pressed under the corner of the desk.

I remember them saying not to keep investigating, but some things make more noise at night the more they are covered up.

April 9, 1981

If someone reads this, go find the blue-covered record book first.

The record book itself is not important. What matters is the paper tucked inside the last page.

textBlocks.content:
April 17, 1981

The road north of the factory is narrow. After the rain, the mud sticks to the soles of your shoes, and each step feels heavier than the last.

They all say there is nothing worth seeing up there, but I always feel that when a person stands higher, the heart can loosen a little.

April 23, 1981

From the mountaintop, the whole mill can be seen at once. At dusk, the lights turn on one by one, as if someone has left the unfinished words of the day inside the night.

If I have another chance, I want to go up there and see it again.
